manual.title: Instruction Manual
manual.subtitle: Complete guide to using Max7 Vista

overview.heading: What is Max7 Vista?
overview.body: Max7 Vista is a clinical patient image management system designed for healthcare professionals. It enables secure capture, organization, and editing of patient photographs and medical images, with support for multiple organizations (tenants), role-based access control, and multilingual operation.

gettingStarted.heading: Getting Started
gettingStarted.body: After logging in, you will see the main navigation sidebar on the left. Use it to navigate between Patients, Capture, Gallery, Settings, and this Manual. Your role (User, Admin, or Super Admin) determines which features are accessible.

patients.heading: Managing Patients
patients.body: Navigate to the Patients section to create, search, edit, or delete patient records. Each patient has a name, patient code, optional date of birth, and notes. Click a patient card to view their full profile and image gallery.

capture.heading: Capturing Images
capture.body: Use the Capture page to take photos directly from your webcam or upload existing files. Select the patient before saving. After capture, you will be taken directly to the Image Editor to annotate and review.

gallery.heading: Gallery & Grid Views
gallery.body: The Gallery shows all images across all patients or filtered by a specific patient. Use the grid selector to display 1, 2, 4, or 8 images per row. Click any image to open it in the editor.

editor.heading: Image Editing
editor.body: The Image Editor provides tools for cropping, zooming, rotating, freehand drawing, and erasing. Arrow: draw directional arrows highlighting clinical structures. Circle: draw circles marking areas of interest. Text labels: place anywhere on the image and drag to reposition in Pointer mode — multiple annotations of any type are supported. Eyedropper: sample a colour from the image for annotations. Ruler: draw measurement lines; Measure mode calibrates real-world scale (mm/px); Resize mode resizes the image so a landmark line matches a reference measurement. Angle: measure the angle formed by two lines — click three points. Overlay: pick any other patient image as a semi-transparent layer for visual comparison; when selected, a secondary toolbar below the main toolbar provides Opacity, Scale (10%–300%), and X/Y position controls with Reset. Smooth (Wand): smooth freehand strokes. Select: rectangle or freehand region to cut, copy, or move. Use the colour picker to change annotation colour. Save persists all edits to disk. Save as Copy creates a new image without modifying the original.

bulkImport.heading: Bulk Image Import
bulkImport.body: The Bulk Import page lets you migrate an existing image archive into Max7 Vista in one step. Two modes are available. Upload ZIP: pack your images into a ZIP file and upload it from any device. Server Folder: on the LAN or desktop version, enter the full server path to the folder containing your images (e.g. /data/photos) and the server reads them directly — no ZIP required. In both modes, the immediate subfolders must be named with the patient ID (e.g. 2116/, 2117/). A single root wrapper folder is detected and skipped automatically. Optionally attach a CSV file with columns id, name, and dateOfBirth to populate patient details; without a CSV, patients are created using the folder name as both ID and name. Capture dates are read from EXIF metadata, falling back to the file modification timestamp. After import, a summary shows patients created, patients matched, images imported, and any files skipped with reasons. Re-importing with a corrected CSV will update the name and date of birth on existing patients without creating duplicates.

documents.heading: Patient Documents
documents.body: Every patient record includes a Documents section where you can store any type of file — Word documents, PDFs, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, images, videos, and audio files. Click the Upload button or drag-and-drop files directly onto the panel to attach them. To read a document without downloading it, click the eye icon: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files open inside the Microsoft Office Online viewer; PDFs open in the browser's built-in PDF reader; images display inline; video and audio files play with standard media controls. The download button is always available on every file. All documents are stored in persistent cloud storage and remain accessible across sessions and deployments.

settings.heading: Settings & Storage
settings.body: Configure the root storage directory for patient images. In the desktop (Electron) version, a folder browser is available. The Directory Indexing section lets you scan the storage folder to register images that are on disk but not yet in the database — useful after manually copying files or restoring a backup. The scan infers the patient from the folder structure ({patientId}/{date}/image.jpg). Images that cannot be matched to a patient are marked Unassigned and can be linked manually from the Gallery. Files already in the database are skipped.

roles.heading: User Roles
roles.body: Max7 Vista supports three roles: User (can view and capture images), Admin (can manage patients, users, and settings within their organization), and Super Admin (full system access across all tenants).

tenants.heading: Multi-Tenant Setup
tenants.body: Each organization using Max7 Vista operates as an independent tenant. Data is fully isolated between tenants. Super Admins can create and manage tenants, while Admins manage their own organization's data and users.

presentations.heading: Presentations
presentations.body: Build clinical slide presentations from patient images. Open Presentations in the sidebar to view or create presentations. Each presentation contains one or more slides, each linked to a patient image with its annotations and an optional caption. Use the slide editor to arrange content, then enter full-screen Presentation mode to display slides to a patient or colleague. Presentations can be patient-specific (created from a patient profile) or cross-patient (accessible from the Presentations hub).

migration.heading: Migration (LAN ↔ Web)
migration.body: Super Admins can transfer all data between the Electron desktop/LAN version and the cloud web version without data loss. Go to Settings → Migration. Click 'Download migration archive' to export a ZIP containing all patient records, image files, users (with encrypted passwords), and system settings. On the destination system, upload that ZIP using 'Import archive'. Existing patients and users are automatically skipped to prevent duplicates. The storage directory setting is intentionally excluded to preserve each system's own file paths. All export and import actions are recorded in the Audit Log.

templates.heading: Templates
templates.body: The Templates feature lets you design reusable print layouts for patient documents. Each template defines a page size (Letter, A4, Legal, or custom), an optional clinic name and address, and one or more picture frames positioned anywhere on the page. Open Templates in the sidebar to create or manage templates. Click 'New Template' to set the title, page size, and clinic info, then click 'Create & Design' to open the Layout Designer. In the designer, click 'Add' to place frames on the page — drag them to move, drag the corner handles to resize, and set a label for each frame in the side panel. Save the template when done. To fill a template, click 'Create Document' on any template card, select an optional patient, and give the document a title. In the Document view, click an empty frame to pick a patient image for that slot, then drag the image to reposition it within the frame. The clinic header block is fully movable and resizable — drag it anywhere on the print canvas to reposition it, and drag its right edge to change the width. Use the Header: On/Off toggle button in the toolbar to include or exclude the clinic header on a per-document basis. The header position, size, and visibility are saved with the document. Click Print to send the finished layout to the printer.

imageLibrary.heading: Image Library
imageLibrary.body:
The Image Library is a standalone repository for decorative, non-clinical images — title slides, landscapes, section headers, clinic branding — that staff upload once and reuse across presentations. It is entirely separate from the patient Gallery; nothing here is linked to a patient record.

To upload, click 'Upload Images' in the top-right corner, or drag and drop image files directly onto the grid. Multiple files can be uploaded at once. A progress percentage is shown during the upload.

Each uploaded image can be given a descriptive title: hover over a thumbnail and click the pencil icon to edit it. The title appears as a label at the bottom of the thumbnail.

To include images in a presentation, click one or more thumbnails to select them (a blue checkmark appears and a selection count is shown in the header). Then click 'Add to Presentation' to open the assignment dialog — choose an existing presentation from the list or select 'New Presentation' and enter a title to create one on the spot. The selected images are added as individual slides.

To delete an image, hover over its thumbnail and click the red trash icon. This permanently removes both the file from storage and the database record and cannot be undone.

exportImages.heading: Exporting Patient Images
exportImages.body: Admins and Super Admins can export one or more images for any patient as a ZIP archive. Open a patient detail page, click the ⋮ (More) menu in the top-right corner, and choose "Export Images". A dialog lists all images for that patient — all are pre-selected by default. Tick or untick individual images, or use "Select All" / "Deselect All". Click "Download ZIP" to generate and download the archive. The file is named with the patient code and today’s date; each entry inside is named with its ID, capture date, and original filename. The export is recorded in the Audit Log. This option is hidden from regular users.

auditLog.heading: Audit Log
auditLog.body: The Audit Log (Administration → Audit Log) is an admin-only section that records all significant system actions: logins, login failures, logouts, patient record creates/edits/deletes, image uploads and views, library asset management, bulk imports, and migrations. Each entry shows the timestamp, the acting user's username, the action type, the affected resource type and ID, any relevant details, and the originating IP address. Use the filters at the top to narrow results by action keyword, username, or date range, then click Apply. The total entry count and pagination controls are shown at the bottom when there are more than 50 entries. The audit log supports HIPAA compliance by maintaining a tamper-evident record of data access and modifications.

sessionTimeout.heading: Session Idle Timeout
sessionTimeout.body: For HIPAA compliance (§164.312(a)(2)(iii)), Max7 Vista automatically logs you out after 15 minutes of inactivity. A warning dialog appears with a 2-minute countdown. Click 'Stay signed in' to reset the timer, or 'Sign out' to end your session immediately. The server also enforces a 30-minute rolling session — each request resets the clock, so active use keeps you signed in. On mobile, returning to the app after 15 minutes in the background will also trigger an automatic logout.

patientAccess.heading: Per-Patient Access Control
patientAccess.body: Admins can restrict regular users to a specific set of patients. In Administration → User Management, click the 'Access' button next to any user with the 'User' role. A dialog lists all patients — tick the ones this user should see. Leaving all boxes unchecked grants that user access to all patients (unrestricted). Admins and Super Admins are always unrestricted and cannot be restricted. The access restriction applies to the patient list, patient detail page, image gallery, capture, documents, and every other patient-specific view. Restrictions take effect immediately without requiring a logout.

bulkImport.title: Bulk Import
bulkImport.subtitle: Import an existing image archive into the system in one step.
bulkImport.zipStep1Body: Pack your image folder into a ZIP. The top-level subfolders must be named with the patient ID (e.g. 2116/photo1.jpg). A single root wrapper folder is detected and skipped automatically (e.g. foto/2116/photo1.jpg works too).
bulkImport.zipStep2Body: A spreadsheet with at least an id column matching the folder names. Optional columns: name, dateOfBirth. Without a CSV, patients are created using the folder name as both ID and name.
bulkImport.zipStep3Body: Capture dates are read from EXIF metadata (DateTimeOriginal), falling back to the ZIP modification timestamp. The filename (without extension) becomes the image legend.
bulkImport.selectFilesDesc: ZIP archive is required; CSV is optional.
bulkImport.hintZipInput: Root → Patient ID folder → image files
bulkImport.folderNoZipBody: Enter the full path to a folder that already exists on the server. The server reads the images directly from disk without any upload.
bulkImport.folderStructureBody: The immediate subfolders of the path you enter must be named with the patient ID (e.g. /data/photos/2116/). A single root wrapper folder is detected and skipped automatically (e.g. /data/photos/foto/2116/ also works).
bulkImport.folderCsvBody: Provide a CSV with id, name, and optionally dateOfBirth columns to populate patient records. Without a CSV, patients are created using the folder name as both ID and name.
bulkImport.folderOriginalsBody: Images are copied into the Max7 Vista storage directory. Your source folder is never modified.
bulkImport.configureDesc: Enter the server folder path. The CSV is optional.
bulkImport.folderPathHint: This path must be accessible by the Max7 Vista server process.
